name: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL 120B-A12B
pitch: NVIDIA's 120B hybrid Mamba2 and mixture-of-experts model, from our EXL3 packs or NVIDIA's NVFP4 checkpoint, text only.
architecture: 88 layers, 40 Mamba2, 40 mixture-of-experts (512 experts a layer, 22 a token, one shared, a 1,024-wide latent) and 8 attention layers without positional encoding, plus a one-step MTP head; it thinks in a <think> block and calls tools in the XML form. Text only in TandemLLM so far (the image tower is not served).
license: The model's license (OpenMDW-1.1) is on its Hugging Face page. TandemLLM itself is AGPL-3.0 or commercial.

devices.label: NVIDIA DGX Spark (128 GB unified memory)
devices.note: The GPU and the CPU share this memory. MemTotal reads 121.6 GiB of the 128 GB.

assets.label: LiLiCorr drafter for Nemotron 3.5 Super VL (NVIDIA)
assets.source: Public on Hugging Face, NVIDIA's NVFP4 drafter (its own NVFP4 head over the target's vocabulary); the engine reads it as stored (engine/drafters/lilicorr.py).

assets.label: Qwen3.5-2B (the narrator, and Wren)
assets.source: Public on Hugging Face; install.sh --setup downloads it for Wren, the fetch step when the narrator is on (VIS-153).

assets.label: Laya decision models
assets.source: Public on Hugging Face (no token needed); the fetch step downloads its three models when Laya is on (VIS-153). Its Python files are not downloaded.

profiles.label: EXL3 4.0 bpw

quality.source: this engine against the BF16 checkpoint's logits (tools/nh_quality.py, 8 wikitext-2 rows of 1,024 tokens from an HF job, BF16 ppl 3.84)

profiles.note: Converted from the BF16 checkpoint (revision 97e00975) by exllamav3 1.6.2 with our Puzzle/Bolt and Super VL patches: every projection at 4 bits, head 6, the MTP head at 4; the vision tower is in the pack in BF16 and not loaded. Measured 2026-10-16: 58.35 GiB at load (59.75 with the MTP head), decode 31.3 tok/s (NVIDIA's NVFP4 19.6). Drafts with NVIDIA's LiLiCorr drafter for Super VL and the lookup. The Hugging Face repository is public: a download needs no token.

profiles.label: EXL3 2.0 bpw experts, 4-bit dense

quality.source: this engine against the BF16 checkpoint's logits (tools/nh_quality.py, 8 wikitext-2 rows of 1,024 tokens from an HF job, BF16 ppl 3.84)

profiles.note: Converted from the BF16 checkpoint (revision 97e00975) by exllamav3 1.6.2 with our Puzzle/Bolt and Super VL patches at 2 bits with -hq (Bolt's 2.0 recipe): routed experts at 2 bits, every other projection at 4, head 6, the MTP head at 4 to 6; the vision tower is in the pack in BF16 and not loaded. Measured 2026-10-16: 31.24 GiB at load, decode 36.8 tok/s (the 4.0 pack 31.4) at a much larger loss (KL 0.325 against 0.049). Drafts with NVIDIA's LiLiCorr drafter for Super VL and the lookup. The Hugging Face repository is public: a download needs no token.

profiles.label: NVFP4 (NVIDIA's checkpoint)

quality.source: this engine against the BF16 checkpoint's logits (tools/nh_quality.py, 8 wikitext-2 rows of 1,024 tokens from an HF job, BF16 ppl 3.84)

profiles.note: NVIDIA's ModelOpt checkpoint read as stored: routed and shared experts NVFP4, the Mamba2 and attention projections and the head FP8 with a tensor scale; activations and the KV cache bf16. A decode token reads 10.1 GB of it. Measured 2026-10-16: 66.63 GiB at load, decode 19.6 tok/s; 131,072 tokens. Drafts with NVIDIA's LiLiCorr drafter and the lookup.

measurements.method: the prose, chat and code asks of tools/fn_lookup_ab.py, one request at a time through one fresh server a run on the DGX Spark, the GPU to itself: greedy, thinking off, 512 new tokens, streamed; decode tok/s = (tokens - 1) / (last token - first token) on the client clock. The profile's drafting (LiLiCorr and the lookup cut by StairCut, the shipped price file with its spec prior), 3 slots, conductor raw, the suffix store off, max_len 140,000. Three runs a cell, alternating with plain servers; every drafted text is the plain run's, and no request was answered from a cache. Measured on the branch merged as 0.11.0 before its version bump (its /health reads 0.10.0): the engine, server and tools are the release's byte for byte. Not measured yet: sampled, 128 tokens, long context, first-token times. Raw data: models/nemotron-3.5-super-vl-120b-a12b/measurements/0.11.0-summary.json.

parts.label: Engine state, the decode graphs and warm-up
parts.source: an estimate until measured on Super VL (Lightning BF16: 1.4)

parts.label: Allocator reserve
parts.source: an estimate until measured on the Spark

per_window_parts.label: Prefill workspace (a 4,096-token chunk's activations, the SSD chunks and the batched experts)

components.label: Conductor
components.what: Gives each request the right instructions and helper packages, and watches long sessions so they do not get stuck.
components.note: On by default, with the model fit LFM2.5 measured (Laya answers the class question, core skill only, no effort sentences, rules or memory notes) until it is measured on NemotronH.

components.label: Narrator
components.what: A small model that writes short status lines while the big model thinks, so you can see what it is doing.
components.note: Qwen3.5-2B, 3.60 GiB in the live memory split. Off by default under Super VL (the model has the box to itself).

components.label: Laya decision models
components.what: Three tiny classifiers that answer the conductor's quick questions, like what kind of request this is, in milliseconds.
components.note: The class question's answer under the model fit (served_classifier off).

components.label: Response cache
components.what: Answers an identical greedy request again from memory, without running the model.
components.note: Off on the reference box. Useful for scripts that send the same request many times; never for a benchmark.

components.label: Other backends
components.what: Lets the dashboard send some model names to other servers or cloud APIs, beside this engine.
components.note: You add the backends later, on the Backends screen.

components.label: Conversation cache
components.what: Keeps the conversation the model is in, so the next turn starts where the last one ended instead of reading everything again.
components.note: The resident prefix with its anchors every 4,096 tokens (the prefill's chunk), the end anchor, the pin and the park; an anchor is 194.3 MiB (162.3 MiB of Mamba2 states and 4,096 tokens of KV at 8,192 bytes, as on Bolt).

components.label: State store
components.what: Saves the model's state after short chats, so the same start a second time costs nothing.

methods.label: Temperature
methods.what: How random the answers are when a client does not say. NVIDIA's generation config sets 1.0.

methods.label: Top-p
methods.what: The share of probability a sampled answer draws from, when a client does not say.

methods.label: Default answer length
methods.what: The longest answer, in tokens, when a client does not set max_tokens.

methods.label: Request time limit
methods.what: Seconds one request may run before the engine stops it.

methods.label: Queue length
methods.what: How many requests may wait for a free slot before new ones are turned away.

methods.label: Queue wait
methods.what: Seconds a request may wait in the queue before it gets an error.

advanced.label: Port
advanced.what: The port the API and the dashboard answer on.

advanced.label: Listen on
advanced.what: The whole network, or only this machine.

advanced.label: Raw engine name
advanced.what: The model name of the raw engine. With the conductor on, clients see TandemLLM and this name is a hidden alias.

advanced.label: Dashboard login
advanced.what: With an admin password set, on makes the dashboard ask for it too.

advanced.label: Admin password
advanced.what: Without one, anyone who reaches the port can change the setup. Generate writes a random one into secrets.env on the box; read it there with cat.
